sn47.4:1.1: This village is possibly connected to the Śālagrāma famed in later years as the origin of the ammonite stones found on the Gaṇḍakī river and worshiped as aniconic forms of Vishnu. Against this theory is that Śālagrāma is too far to the north-east, although in truth we do not know the exact extent of Kosala. The feminine ending of the Pali form suggests that the name means “hall”, but Sanskrit sources trace Śālagrāma to the sal trees that grow abundantly in the Himalayan foothills. | The same framing narrative recurs at MN 60, where the topic of rebirth is also discussed.
sn47.4:2.1: Traditionally, new monastics are taught the meditation on parts of the body (MN 10:10.1, Kp 3:1.1). See too AN 5.114.
sn47.4:3.1: Through the practice of mindfulness meditation they have attained jhāna and now seek to deepen understanding.
sn47.4:4.1: The arahants continue to meditate, not in order to achieve anything, but simply because it is a pure and blissful abiding.
